item.title: Iran war hits 6-month mark with no end in sight
item.description: President Trump insists Iran is "begging to make a deal" to end the war, but Tehran, and crucially China, say his economic warfare tactics will fail.

item.title: Couple recounts surviving deadly Nepal flood: "I knew I was going to die"
item.description: A California couple were in a Nepali village when an avalanche of powerful waters ripped down from the high Himalayas toward them.

item.title: Tennis stars prepare for 2026 U.S. Open with Venus and Serena Williams set to play doubles
item.description: Dan Wolken, senior writer for Yahoo Sports, joins CBS News to preview the upcoming U.S. Open tennis tournament.

item.title: Thousands march in Washington for Defend the Vote rally
item.description: Sixty-three years after the March on Washington, thousands gathered Friday in the nation's capitol for a Defend the Vote rally and warned that voting rights are under attack again. Earlier this year, the Supreme Court weakened a key provision of the Voting Rights Act of 1965, making it harder for people to challenge voting maps they argued were racially discriminatory. Tylik McMillan, national director of youth and college for the NAACP and one of the speakers at Friday's march, joins CBS News to talk about the day.

item.title: Trump says U.S. now has control of over 60 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil reserves
item.description: President Trump announced a deal to grant the U.S. control of more than 60 billion barrels of proven Venezuelan oil reserves.

item.title: How a chance encounter gave a struggling ex-football star a new lease on life
item.description: On a path in Austin, Texas, a chance meeting changed the lives of two men with one thing in common.

item.title: Good Good Golf's very bad, bad week amid backlash over Callaway ad
item.description: Good Good Golf will no longer sponsor an upcoming PGA tournament, while Callaway said it has ended its partnership with the company.

item.title: Judge rules Trump administration illegally punished Anthropic
item.description: A judge has blocked the Trump administration from blacklisting artificial intelligence company Anthropic. Earlier this year, President Trump ordered federal agencies to stop using Anthropic's Claude AI assistant. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth also declared the company a supply chain risk. These moves came after the company refused to allow the military to use its tech for mass surveillance or autonomous weapons. CBS News legal contributor Jessica Levinson breaks down the constitutionality of the ruling.

item.title: How a chance meeting changed the life of a former star college athelete turned homeless
item.description: An Indiana University alum was surprised to see a homeless man wearing a branded backpack from his school. When he approached him, their lives changed forever. Steve Hartman takes us on the road.

item.title: Callaway, Good Good Golf in crisis as shocking ad shows man shoving woman to the ground
item.description: Callaway and Good Good Golf are facing backlash over a co-branded ad featuring a man shoving a woman to the ground for touching his golf club. Mark Strassman reports.

item.title: Nashville airport could be renamed for Dolly Parton under new proposal
item.description: The international airport in Nashville, Tennessee, would be renamed for Dolly Parton under a proposal by Tennessee's governor.

item.title: Marine One has trouble communicating with air traffic control again
item.description: The incident happened about an hour after the National Transportation Safety Board released new details​ about a similar incident in early August.

item.title: Tennessee governor announces plan to rename Nashville airport for Dolly Parton
item.description: In the days since her death, Dolly Parton has become the most-streamed artist in the world and might be getting an airport named after her. Nicole Valdes has more.

item.title: Closing arguments expected Monday in Tupac murder trial
item.description: Attorneys finalized jury instructions with the judge Friday after witness testimony wrapped Thursday in the trial of Duane Davis, also known as "Keefe D," who's accused of orchestrating the drive-by shooting that killed Tupac Shakur in 1996. Davis has denied the allegations. CBS News' Katrina Kaufman has more.

item.title: Trump's Marine One helicopter faces second air traffic control security threat this month
item.description: President Trump's Marine One helicopter was involved in a new communication incident involving air traffic control, the second this month. Kris Van Cleave has the story.

item.title: People who survived disastrous Nepal flooding recount thinking they were going to die
item.description: Close to 600 people have died, and more than 90 Americans are still missing after catastrophic flooding and mudslides hit Nepal this week. Ramy Inocencio reports.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy scared and sad as jury deliberations pause for the weekend, her attorney says
item.description: The jury in the trial of Lindsay Clancy, the woman accused of murdering her three young children, is still deliberating on whether to accept her postpartum psychosis defense. Shanelle Kaul reports and Caroline Polisi provides legal analysis.

item.title: 6 months into the Iran war, here's where things stand
item.description: CBS News national security contributor Samantha Vinograd takes a look at the current state of the Iran war, six months after the fighting began.

item.title: Milo Yiannopoulos is in ICE custody facing a final removal order, sources say
item.description: A Department of Homeland Security spokesperson said Milo Yiannopoulos "chose to overstay his welcome."

item.title: ICE arrests right-wing commentator Milo Yiannopoulos, labels him an "illegal alien"
item.description: British right-wing political commentator Milo Yiannopoulos, who supported President Trump's agenda, is being held by ICE for allegedly overstaying his visa. Nancy Cordes has the details.

item.title: Trump signs executive order to create a U.S. Space Academy
item.description: "Space is the hot thing," President Trump said at the NASA Johnson Space Center in Houston.

item.title: Labor Day travelers to face higher costs, heavier traffic, AAA says
item.description: People who are flying to their destinations this Labor Day will face steep prices, according to AAA. Flights to top domestic destinations cost about 21% more than last year and travelers hitting the roads will face higher costs for gas. The national average is up 27% over last year. Sean Cudahy, senior aviation reporter for The Points Guy, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: CENTCOM says Strait of Hormuz is open, shipping companies not convinced as Iran war hits 6 months
item.description: Adm. Brad Cooper, head of U.S. Central Command, says the Strait of Hormuz is open again, six months into the war with Iran, but the shipping industry is skeptical. CBS News' Charlie D'Agata and Nana-Séntuo Bonsu have the latest.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy protesters and supporters gather outside courthouse as deliberations continue
item.description: Jurors went home for the weekend Friday with deliberations set to resume Monday morning in the trial of Lindsay Clancy. Clancy has admitted to killing her three young children, but is arguing she was suffering from postpartum psychosis. CBS News' Shanelle Kaul has more.

item.title: Judge again rejects Trump's bid to erase his New York hush money conviction
item.description: A federal judge has again blocked President Trump's bid to erase his hush money conviction in New York.

item.title: How national security threats have evolved in 25 years since 9/11
item.description: As the world approaches 25 years since the 9/11 attacks, the House Intelligence Committee has a new report on emerging threats in the era of artificial intelligence. The committee's chair, GOP Rep. Rick Crawford of Arkansas, joins "The Takeout" with the first look.

item.title: H. R. McMaster says economic pressure on Iran will "make a big difference" as war hits 6-month mark
item.description: Six months into the Iran war, newly aggressive U.S. economic sanctions against Tehran are raising alarms in the Middle East as banks scramble to avoid or minimize their impact. Former Trump national security adviser H. R. McMaster joins with his perspective.

item.title: Court hands states a win in fight over who regulates prediction markets
item.description: Trading of sports event contracts on Kalshi constitutes gambling, appeals court rules in siding with Nevada officials.

item.title: 8/28: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Iran war hits 6-month mark with negotiations stalled; Lindsay Clancy jury ends Day 2 of deliberations without a verdict.

item.title: Dolly Parton offered to try experimental drugs if "no hope" in her cancer battle
item.description: Stella Parton said her sister Dolly told her "that if there was no hope for her, she would still allow her medical team to try experimental drugs in the hope of helping others in the future."
